headline: Dengue surge: Four more die, 1,631 hospitalized in 24 hours
summary: Total deaths this year have risen to 299 as thousands of patients continue to undergo treatment across the country.
details: At least four dengue patients died and 1,631 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am today.
The deaths were reported across four different regions: Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC), Barishal, Chattogram, and Khulna divisions.
With these latest figures, the total number of dengue deaths this year has risen to 299, while total cases have reached 97,082.
Currently, 5,776 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across Bangladesh.

headline_marked: Detained CJP leader [[Abhijeet Dipke given choice to attend grandmother's funeral]]
headline: Detained CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke given choice to attend grandmother's funeral
summary: Delhi Police informed the Cockroach Janta Party founder of his grandmother's death while he was in custody ahead of a planned protest.
details: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was detained at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday morning as he arrived to participate in a planned protest.
While in custody, Delhi Police informed Dipke that his 85-year-old paternal grandmother, Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, had passed away at her home in Maharashtra's Hingoli district.
Police sources stated that Dipke can now decide whether to remain in Delhi to continue the protest under detention or return home to attend his grandmother's last rites scheduled for Sunday morning.
Dipke and two other CJP members, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained as they arrived in the capital to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The protest, planned for Jantar Mantar, was aimed at highlighting alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls across India.
Dipke's family in Maharashtra has been unable to contact him due to his detention, and his parents are currently under police surveillance at their residence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.
caption:
A detained political leader is faced with a heartbreaking choice: stay in custody for a protest or return home for his grandmother's funeral.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was detained at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday morning as he arrived to participate in a planned protest.

While in custody, Delhi Police informed Dipke that his 85-year-old paternal grandmother, Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, had passed away at her home in Maharashtra's Hingoli district.

Police sources stated that Dipke can now decide whether to remain in Delhi to continue the protest under detention or return home to attend his grandmother's last rites scheduled for Sunday morning.

Dipke and two other CJP members, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained as they arrived in the capital to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The protest, planned for Jantar Mantar, was aimed at highlighting alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls across India.

Dipke's family in Maharashtra has been unable to contact him due to his detention, and his parents are currently under police surveillance at their residence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

#India #DelhiPolice #CJP #AbhijeetDipke #HumanRights #News

Source: The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, bdnews24.com
